items.title: @fiiiiiist：Big new IFP report from @GeorgiaCAdamson, @KonstantinPilz, and me on the US-China AI competition. We spent the last 6 mo
items.abstract_or_text: Big new IFP report from @GeorgiaCAdamson, @KonstantinPilz, and me on the US-China AI competition. We spent the last 6 months digging into how Chinese AI companies’ access to compute and distillation of American models translate into the current US-China capabilities gap. The result is a 23k-word research report, including an interactive analytical model that visualizes changes in the US AI lead under different policy interventions. Our findings: 1. The US AI lead over China is currently only around 6 months. 2. The US could roughly double this lead, to over a year, using authorities already available to the federal government. 3. On chips: China’s access to AI chips will roughly double over the next year, with chips housed in data centers overseas accounting for roughly half of China’s 2027 compute. 4. On distillation: the current ~16x US training compute advantage would normally yield a 13-month lead. But we estimate adversarial distillation halves this to around 6.5 months.

items.title: @Math_files：Mathematicians Repair a Major Graph Theory Theorem With AI-Assisted Formal Verification Four mathematicians, James Davie
items.abstract_or_text: Mathematicians Repair a Major Graph Theory Theorem With AI-Assisted Formal Verification Four mathematicians, James Davies, Paweł Rzążewski, Jack Spalding-Jamieson, and Bartosz Walczak, have presented a new proof of an important theorem in graph theory, addressing a flaw discovered in 2024 in an earlier argument concerning string graphs, which represent intersections of curves in the plane. An interesting aspect of the research is the carefully documented role of artificial intelligence. The authors explicitly state that the principal mathematical results were obtained entirely by the human researchers, while AI systems contributed substantially to their formal verification. In particular, the AI theorem prover Aristotle generated almost all of the Lean 4 formalizations of two principal results. GPT-5.6 Sol also assisted in formalizing an improved bound and contributed an initial version of that improvement.

items.abstract_or_text: What's still very hard: theory of mind. The world, the voices and the mechanics were great. Writing the story was the weak part: the model assumes the player knows more than they do, and its NPC sometimes react in strange way or to things that never happened. A Diamond Age's Primer (or any real AI tutor fwiw) will have to model the learner, and that is where it still falls short in a default setting imo. I've actually started exploring benchmarks on this and it's a hard task for LLMs right now. They are prone to the "Curse of knowledge". Teaching humans is also not very much a Verifiable Reward, so it's hard to scale within the current training paradigm.
